paras: The reported lynching near Orchard Hill, Georgia, was the hanging by a mob of an unnamed Black man accused of assaulting a white woman near Orchard Hill on September 12, 1881. The hanging appears in only one report, a telegraphic brief in the Washington National Republican; other printings of the same Atlanta dispatch said only that the man had been arrested and identified.

According to an Atlanta dispatch dated September 13, a white woman "was outraged by a negro yesterday near Orchard Hill." The Savannah Morning News, printing the same item, placed the alleged assault on "Monday." The dispatch added that the man "has since been arrested and identified by the woman," without saying who arrested him or where he was held.

The National Republican's version of the brief, printed on September 14, went further and said that after his arrest and identification he had been "hanged by a mob." No paper named the man, the woman, those who arrested him or any member of the mob, and none described where, when or how the hanging was carried out.
No report of an inquest, of arrests of mob members, or of any later news from Orchard Hill appears in the coverage.

The story circulated only as a one- or two-sentence item in news-summary columns, and every version identified the parties solely by race, as "a white woman" and "a negro," while stating the accusation as fact. The Evening Star ran the Atlanta dispatch on September 13 under the headline "A Georgia Tragedy," which it shared with a report of a man killed on the Air-Line railroad track. The next day the Savannah Morning News printed it among its briefs, while the National Republican listed its fuller version, hanging included, among its "Telegraphic Twistings" without comment.
Shortened versions that dropped the date and ended with the arrest later ran in The People's Advocate of Washington on September 17 and the Stephens City Star of Virginia on September 24.

The accounts differ on the outcome: the National Republican said the man was hanged by a mob, while the Evening Star and the Savannah Morning News ended with his arrest and identification. None of the reports denied a hanging, and the coverage does not show whether the National Republican's addition came from a later dispatch.

reader.title: Reported lynching near Orchard Hill, Georgia
bases: The only report of an outcome beyond arrest says the accused man was 'hanged by a mob' after he was arrested and identified (A2); the other versions stop at the arrest (A1, A3).

The National Republican reported that a Black man accused of outraging a white woman was hanged by a mob after his arrest and identification, which meets each part of the definition (A2). It is the only report of the hanging; the same Atlanta dispatch in other papers mentions only the arrest (A1, A3), so the killing rests on a single source.

The accusation and arrest are reported in several printings of one Atlanta dispatch (A1, A3), but the hanging appears only in the National Republican (A2) and no independent or local account confirms it.
